M-02 Customer Selectors in Trait With
interface_id Attribute Are Not Checked in
Implementation
The #[interface_id] attribute is implemented as a procedural macro that can be added to
a trait. This macro re-generates the trait source code with the addition of an interface_id
function to produce its ERC-165 identifier.
The macro consumes any #[selector] attributes within the trait, allowing them to exist in
traits. Within the Stylus SDK, the #[selector] attribute may only exist within #[public]
blocks and does not provide logic for the macro within traits. However, there is no mechanism
in place to enforce that trait implementations match the interface of traits with custom
selectors.
As a consequence, developers must remember to add any custom selectors in trait
implementations to correctly support the interface identifier, and there are no checks to ensure
this. As a result, the ABI for a particular implementation may not match its trait, violating
assumed invariants within Rust and potentially leading to failed contract integrations.
Consider refactoring the implementation of the interface_id macro to verify compatibility
in custom selectors with respective trait implementations.
Update: Acknowledged, will resolve. The Contracts for Stylus team stated:
We have recommended the Stylus SDK team to include the #[interface_id]
functionality and the option to retrieve selectors of each method and auto-implement
each router function to build inheritance this way (Doing so would allow compile-time
checks on custom selector differences between traits and implementation). We will work
with the team to add this functionality in future iterations.

Low Severity
L-01 Verification Functions for Custom Hashing in
Merkle Trees Assume Commutative Hashing
The functions verify_with_builder and verify_multi_proof_with_builder serve as verifiers for
Merkle trees with custom hashing functions. However, these functions reconstruct the Merkle

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Low Severity − 11

 root in a commutative manner, which assumes that all custom hashing algorithms employ
commutative hashing. Although commutative hashing is common practice, this assumption
cannot be guaranteed for all custom hashing processes.
Consider updating the documentation to specify that the Merkle tree hashing process must be
constructed commutatively when using custom hashing algorithms.
Update: Resolved in pull #674 at commit 6f75f80.

L-02 Inconsistent Data Types for carry and
borrow Parameters
The arithmetic carry (for addition) and borrow (for subtraction) parameters are defined as the
Limb type in the adc and sbb functions, but as the bool type in the adc_assign and
sbb_assign functions. These parameters are currently expected to hold only the values 0 or
1 , as required by the functions that utilize them. However, unintended behavior may arise if a
function erroneously passes a carry or borrow parameter with a value greater than 1.
For example, the overflow protection mechanism will fail if a = 0 , b = u64::MAX , and
borrow = 2 in the sbb function. Consider adopting the bool type exclusively for carry and
borrow parameters, casting them to Limb during calculations as necessary.
Update: Resolved in pull #675 at commit cde91fc.

L-03 Encoding Ambiguity in ct_num_bits
Function
According to the comment of the ct_num_bits function, it returns the minimum number of
bits required to encode a given number. Currently, it returns 0 for the number 0 . However, in
practical encoding scenarios, a minimum of one bit is necessary to represent any number,
including 0 . Returning 0 bits for the number 0 may introduce ambiguity or errors in systems
that expect at least one bit to represent valid numbers. Consider revising the function to ensure
it returns at least one bit for all inputs.
Update: Resolved in pull #681 at commit e36c292.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Low Severity − 12

 L-04 Absence of Overflow Check in
from_str_hex Function
The from_str_hex function does not include an overflow check when parsing hexadecimal
strings into a Uint<LIMBS> type. This omission may result in an unexpected index out-ofbounds panic if the input string represents a number exceeding the capacity of the
Uint<LIMBS> type. In contrast, the from_str_radix function incorporates an overflow
check within the ct_add function, ensuring that overflow conditions are explicitly detected
and trigger a panic with a clear error message.
Consider implementing an overflow check in the from_str_hex function to enhance its
robustness.
Update: Resolved in pull #673 at comit a988e2b.

L-05 Underlying Decimals in Erc20Wrapper Can
Be Set Incorrectly
The Erc20Wrapper contracts set the underlying token address during construction but do
not set the underlying_decimals storage field from the decimals of the underlying token.
The underlying decimals must then be set manually, which can lead to critical errors in token
functionality if the decimals are set incorrectly. Consider assigning the
underlying_decimals field in the constructor using the decimals of the underlying
token, or including checks to ensure the assigned values are equal.
Update: Resolved in pull request #699 at commit add8075.

L-06 State Mutability Can Be Restricted in
IErc4626
The IErc4626 trait currently marks several methods with &mut self even though they only
need to read contract storage, such as total_assets , convert_to_shares ,
convert_to_assets , etc.
By requiring &mut self on methods that are conceptually read-only, the trait allows
implementations to introduce unintended or malicious state changes. This is because a
developer could override a “read-only” function and write to storage. To preserve expected

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Low Severity − 13

 invariants and prevent misuse, consider changing the signature of any IErc4626 method that
does not modify state to take &self rather than &mut self .
Update: Resolved in pull request #698 at commit 33b15ed.

L-07 Custom Selectors in Trait With
interface_id Allows Unreachable Patterns
The #[interface_id] attribute enables custom selectors to be added to function
signatures in traits via the #[selector] attribute. This mirrors the functionality available for
functions within #[public] implementation blocks in the Stylus SDK. Code that includes
functions with identical selectors in #[public] blocks yields an unreachable pattern error;
however, this enforcement is not present in traits with the #[interface_id] . Consequently,
it is possible to define traits with the #[interface_id] attribute that can never be
implemented. To maintain expected programming invariants and reduce developer errors,
consider prohibiting the creation of traits that have duplicate function selectors.
Update: Resolved in pull request #702 at commit b68f7ae.

L-08 Missing Trait Components in Generated
Code From interface_id Macro
The #[interface_id] macro processes a trait by adding an interface_id function to
the trait's re-generated code, maintaining the original content apart from this intentional
addition. However, two critical components are omitted:
1. Generic bounds are missing:
The ty_generics variable expands only to the generic type name without including bounds.
For example, a trait like trait Foo<T: U> would expand to trait Foo<T> . This omission
can allow implementers to create contracts with generic types that do not respect the specified
bounds, potentially violating intended invariants.
1. unsafe qualifier is lost:
Rust allows traits to be declared with the unsafe qualifier, indicating that implementations
may require the use of unsafe features. The loss of this keyword can silently weaken the safety
guarantees intended by the unsafe trait , allowing implementations to compile without the
necessary flag.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Low Severity − 14

 When re-generating a trait in the interface_id macro, it is advisable to include all
declaration components, ensuring that the output precisely replicates the source trait. This
practice prevents implementers from bypassing generic bounds or omitting critical
annotations, thereby preserving both type safety and intended invariants.
Update: Resolved in pull request #705 at commit 184bf10.

L-09 Potential Vulnerability in Big Integer Library
to Timing Side-Channel Attacks
Certain functions like ct_ge(), ct_gt(), and cmp() in the big integer cryptographic library utilize
early returns when comparing values. The use of early returns does not ensure constant-time
execution across all inputs, potentially exposing the library to timing side-channel attacks.
When the input values contain sensitive information, such attacks could enable an attacker to
analyze the execution time to infer details about those values.
#[inline(always)] attribute would ensure consistent inlining behavior, minimize function
call overhead, and enhance performance. Consider adding the #[inline(always)]
attribute to these methods.
Update: Resolved in pull #707 at commit 80402e2.

N-04 Incorrect Comment in PartialEq
Implementation for Projective Points
The comment for the PartialEq implementation of Projective points states that points
(X, Y, Z) and (X', Y', Z') are equal when (X * Z^2) = (X' * Z'^2) and (Y *
Z^3) = (Y' * Z'^3) . However, the implementation verifies
(X * Z'^2) = (X' * Z^2) and (Y * Z'^3) = (Y' * Z^3) , which is correct. The
comment is inaccurate because it fails to reflect the correct order of operations in the
implementation. Consider revising the comment.
Update: Resolved in pull #711 at commit 12adbbc.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Notes & Additional Information − 16

 N-05 Source Code Attribution Concerns
Certain components of the library, such as the curve module, which incorporates code derived
from algebra/ec, and the field module, which utilizes code from algebra/ff, include portions of
code from external codebases without proper attribution. It is recommended to include
references to the original codebases within the code comments to ensure proper attribution.
Update: Resolved at pull #712 at commit eaa0ba2.

N-06 Documentation Enhancements
Two opportunities for enhancing documentation were identified within the codebase:
• The absorb function enforces that the mode is set to Absorbing . However, the
squeeze function permits the mode to remain Absorbing , without a reciprocal check
to ensure the mode is Squeezing . This behavior is correct, as the function should
remain in Squeezing mode until reinitialized.
To enhance clarity, consider adding a comment to the absorb function: "Transitions from
Absorbing to Squeezing mode are unidirectional." This comment emphasizes that once in
Squeezing mode, returning to Absorbing mode is not possible, thereby justifying the ifcondition. Similarly, consider adding a comment to the squeeze function: "When invoked from
Absorbing mode, this function triggers a permutation and transitions to Squeezing mode."
• The Poseidon2 implementation forms part of a low-level library, providing foundational
components for constructing a complete hash function. Consequently, high-level
functionalities, such as padding, domain separation, and absorb/squeeze transitions, are
the responsibility of the library user.
To clarify this, consider amending the documentation with a statement such as: "This interface
does not implement padding or domain separation. Users are responsible for padding inputs,
prepending domain separation tags, and managing absorb/squeeze transitions."
Consider implementing the recommended documentation enhancements to improve clarity
and usability.
Update: Resolved in pull #710 at commit eb72ebc.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Notes & Additional Information − 17

 N-07 Inconsistent Behavior of Shift Overflow
Compared to Rust Native Integer Types
As specified in Rust RFC 560, for a type of width N (for example, u32 where N = 32 ), if the
right-hand operand (shift amount) is greater than or equal to N , it is masked to
shift_amount % N . This ensures the effective shift amount remains within the valid range.
For example:
• Shifting 1u32 << 32 is equivalent to 1u32 << 0 (since 32 % 32 = 0 ), resulting in
1.
• Shifting 1u32 << 33 is equivalent to 1u32 << 1 (since 33 % 32 = 1 ), resulting in
2.
However, the implementation of the shr_assign and shl_assign functions returns Zero
for overflow shifts. This behavior is inconsistent with the default operation of native integer shift
operations in Rust. Consider aligning the implementation with Rust's native behavior to ensure
consistency and predictability.
Update: Resolved in pull #658 at commit c38b883. The shift operation will revert for shift
overflow.

N-08 Misleading Documentation
The #[interface_id] procedural macro is described as adding an associated constant [1,
2], but it is actually added as a function. Consider correcting this comment to reflect accurate
behavior.
Update: Resolved partially in pull request #705 at commit 184bf10 and partially in pull request
#702 at commit b68f7ae.

N-09 Typographical Errors
Throughout the codebase, the following typographical errors were identified:
• The variable " underline_token " should be renamed to " underlying_token ."
• The test " prevents_non_onwers_from_transferring " should be renamed to
"prevents_non_owners_from_transferring."

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Notes & Additional Information − 18

 • In line 111 of contracts/src/access/control.rs , the comment should say, "The
caller of a function..."
Consider correcting these errors and any others within the codebase to improve overall clarity.
Update: Resolved in pull request #709 at commit 917b9e2.

N-10 Insufficient Unit Test Coverage
Certain parts of the codebase lack adequate unit tests. For example, the crypto arithmetic
limb.rs module does not exercise all of its functions. Consider increasing test coverage to
ensure correctness across edge cases.
Update: Acknowledged, will resolve. The team stated:
We will improve test coverage both on crypto and contracts part this during our
Milestone 3.

Recommendations
Recommendations
• Check for Poseidon2 S-box Invertibility: Add a check gcd(P::D, F::MODULUS - 1)
== 1 in the new() function to ensure the invertibility of the S-box mapping
f(x)=x^D .
• Enforce Even Number of Full Rounds and Minimal Number of Rounds in Poseidon2:
According to the Poseidon2 paper, the total number of full rounds must be an even
number. The current implementation assumes this condition is met. Consider adding a
check to ensure that this requirement is enforced. Also, a minimal number of rounds
must be done to achieve the required security parameter.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Recommendations − 19

 Conclusion
The Contracts for Stylus library has been upgraded to leverage the latest Stylus SDK and now
offers a richer, more user-friendly feature set. Notably, it adds a fully integrated ERC-4626 vault
for ERC-20 tokens—an essential building block for DeFi applications—and expands ERC-1155
support with burnable extensions, metadata URI management, and supply controls,
addressing growing NFT use cases. These enhancements significantly broaden the library’s
applicability and demonstrate a clear, well-organized code structure.
The Crypto Library offers a comprehensive suite of cryptographic utilities across six modules,
designed for secure and efficient blockchain applications. It features a generic hash module for
producing larger-size outputs, a merkle module for efficient Merkle proof verification, and an
arithmetic module for safe big integer operations. Additionally, the curve module enables
elliptic curve operations with affine and projective representations, while the field module
supports finite field arithmetic computations. The Poseidon2 and Pedersen modules provide
fast, blockchain-optimized hash functions, tailored for zero-knowledge proofs.
The audit identified one high-severity issue and two medium-severity issues, along with several
low-severity findings and general notes across the contracts and crypto library scopes. To
maintain robust security and feature integrity, regular audits are strongly recommended
whenever major library updates are introduced. Continued development and iteration will
further strengthen the library's utility and contribution to the Arbitrum Stylus ecosystem.

The #[interface_id] macro processes a trait by adding an interface_id function to
the trait's re-generated code, maintaining the original content apart from this intentional
addition. However, two critical components are omitted:
1. Generic bounds are missing:
The ty_generics variable expands only to the generic type name without including bounds.
For example, a trait like trait Foo<T: U> would expand to trait Foo<T> . This omission
can allow implementers to create contracts with generic types that do not respect the specified
bounds, potentially violating intended invariants.
1. unsafe qualifier is lost:
Rust allows traits to be declared with the unsafe qualifier, indicating that implementations
may require the use of unsafe features. The loss of this keyword can silently weaken the safety
guarantees intended by the unsafe trait , allowing implementations to compile without the
necessary flag.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Low Severity − 14

 When re-generating a trait in the interface_id macro, it is advisable to include all
declaration components, ensuring that the output precisely replicates the source trait. This
practice prevents implementers from bypassing generic bounds or omitting critical
annotations, thereby preserving both type safety and intended invariants.
Update: Resolved in pull request #705 at commit 184bf10.

L-09 Potential Vulnerability in Big Integer Library
to Timing Side-Channel Attacks
Certain functions like ct_ge(), ct_gt(), and cmp() in the big integer cryptographic library utilize
early returns when comparing values. The use of early returns does not ensure constant-time
execution across all inputs, potentially exposing the library to timing side-channel attacks.
When the input values contain sensitive information, such attacks could enable an attacker to
analyze the execution time to infer details about those values.
#[inline(always)] attribute would ensure consistent inlining behavior, minimize function
call overhead, and enhance performance. Consider adding the #[inline(always)]
attribute to these methods.
Update: Resolved in pull #707 at commit 80402e2.

N-04 Incorrect Comment in PartialEq
Implementation for Projective Points
The comment for the PartialEq implementation of Projective points states that points
(X, Y, Z) and (X', Y', Z') are equal when (X * Z^2) = (X' * Z'^2) and (Y *
Z^3) = (Y' * Z'^3) . However, the implementation verifies
(X * Z'^2) = (X' * Z^2) and (Y * Z'^3) = (Y' * Z^3) , which is correct. The
comment is inaccurate because it fails to reflect the correct order of operations in the
implementation. Consider revising the comment.
Update: Resolved in pull #711 at commit 12adbbc.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Notes & Additional Information − 16

 N-05 Source Code Attribution Concerns
Certain components of the library, such as the curve module, which incorporates code derived
from algebra/ec, and the field module, which utilizes code from algebra/ff, include portions of
code from external codebases without proper attribution. It is recommended to include
references to the original codebases within the code comments to ensure proper attribution.
Update: Resolved at pull #712 at commit eaa0ba2.

N-06 Documentation Enhancements
Two opportunities for enhancing documentation were identified within the codebase:
• The absorb function enforces that the mode is set to Absorbing . However, the
squeeze function permits the mode to remain Absorbing , without a reciprocal check
to ensure the mode is Squeezing . This behavior is correct, as the function should
remain in Squeezing mode until reinitialized.
To enhance clarity, consider adding a comment to the absorb function: "Transitions from
Absorbing to Squeezing mode are unidirectional." This comment emphasizes that once in
Squeezing mode, returning to Absorbing mode is not possible, thereby justifying the ifcondition. Similarly, consider adding a comment to the squeeze function: "When invoked from
Absorbing mode, this function triggers a permutation and transitions to Squeezing mode."
• The Poseidon2 implementation forms part of a low-level library, providing foundational
components for constructing a complete hash function. Consequently, high-level
functionalities, such as padding, domain separation, and absorb/squeeze transitions, are
the responsibility of the library user.
To clarify this, consider amending the documentation with a statement such as: "This interface
does not implement padding or domain separation. Users are responsible for padding inputs,
prepending domain separation tags, and managing absorb/squeeze transitions."
Consider implementing the recommended documentation enhancements to improve clarity
and usability.
Update: Resolved in pull #710 at commit eb72ebc.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Notes & Additional Information − 17

 N-07 Inconsistent Behavior of Shift Overflow
Compared to Rust Native Integer Types
As specified in Rust RFC 560, for a type of width N (for example, u32 where N = 32 ), if the
right-hand operand (shift amount) is greater than or equal to N , it is masked to
shift_amount % N . This ensures the effective shift amount remains within the valid range.
For example:
• Shifting 1u32 << 32 is equivalent to 1u32 << 0 (since 32 % 32 = 0 ), resulting in
1.
• Shifting 1u32 << 33 is equivalent to 1u32 << 1 (since 33 % 32 = 1 ), resulting in
2.
However, the implementation of the shr_assign and shl_assign functions returns Zero
for overflow shifts. This behavior is inconsistent with the default operation of native integer shift
operations in Rust. Consider aligning the implementation with Rust's native behavior to ensure
consistency and predictability.
Update: Resolved in pull #658 at commit c38b883. The shift operation will revert for shift
overflow.

The #[interface_id] procedural macro is described as adding an associated constant [1,
2], but it is actually added as a function. Consider correcting this comment to reflect accurate
behavior.
Update: Resolved partially in pull request #705 at commit 184bf10 and partially in pull request

• The test " prevents_non_onwers_from_transferring " should be renamed to
"prevents_non_owners_from_transferring."

caller of a function..."
Consider correcting these errors and any others within the codebase to improve overall clarity.
Update: Resolved in pull request #709 at commit 917b9e2.

N-10 Insufficient Unit Test Coverage
Certain parts of the codebase lack adequate unit tests. For example, the crypto arithmetic
limb.rs module does not exercise all of its functions. Consider increasing test coverage to
ensure correctness across edge cases.
Update: Acknowledged, will resolve. The team stated:
We will improve test coverage both on crypto and contracts part this during our
Milestone 3.

Recommendations
Recommendations
• Check for Poseidon2 S-box Invertibility: Add a check gcd(P::D, F::MODULUS - 1)
== 1 in the new() function to ensure the invertibility of the S-box mapping
f(x)=x^D .
• Enforce Even Number of Full Rounds and Minimal Number of Rounds in Poseidon2:
According to the Poseidon2 paper, the total number of full rounds must be an even
number. The current implementation assumes this condition is met. Consider adding a
check to ensure that this requirement is enforced. Also, a minimal number of rounds
must be done to achieve the required security parameter.

Stylus Contracts Library v0.2.0 Audit − Recommendations − 19

 Conclusion
The Contracts for Stylus library has been upgraded to leverage the latest Stylus SDK and now
offers a richer, more user-friendly feature set. Notably, it adds a fully integrated ERC-4626 vault
for ERC-20 tokens—an essential building block for DeFi applications—and expands ERC-1155
support with burnable extensions, metadata URI management, and supply controls,
addressing growing NFT use cases. These enhancements significantly broaden the library’s
applicability and demonstrate a clear, well-organized code structure.
The Crypto Library offers a comprehensive suite of cryptographic utilities across six modules,
designed for secure and efficient blockchain applications. It features a generic hash module for
producing larger-size outputs, a merkle module for efficient Merkle proof verification, and an
arithmetic module for safe big integer operations. Additionally, the curve module enables
elliptic curve operations with affine and projective representations, while the field module
supports finite field arithmetic computations. The Poseidon2 and Pedersen modules provide
fast, blockchain-optimized hash functions, tailored for zero-knowledge proofs.
The audit identified one high-severity issue and two medium-severity issues, along with several
low-severity findings and general notes across the contracts and crypto library scopes. To
maintain robust security and feature integrity, regular audits are strongly recommended
whenever major library updates are introduced. Continued development and iteration will
further strengthen the library's utility and contribution to the Arbitrum Stylus ecosystem.

L-02 Inconsistent Implementations in ERC-721
Extension
The Stylus library ERC-721 extensions are not consistent with the respective functionality of
the Solidity library.
These inconsistencies were identified:
• In the uri_storage extension, the token_uri() function directly returns the value from
storage but omits key checks:
◦ It does not verify whether the token exists, which is handled in the Solidity
implementation.
◦ It does not handle base URI concatenation like the Solidity version. Instead, it
directly retrieves and returns the stored token URI without constructing the full
URI.
• There is a mismatch in the implementation of ERC721Metadata :
◦ The Rust implementation exposes the base_uri function. In the Solidity version,
URIs are only accessible by token ID when the token exists. Not exposing
baseURI is generally advisable, as revealing it prematurely can leak sensitive NFT
data before minting. This can enable advanced users to time their minting to
acquire more desirable NFTs.
◦ The Rust version lacks the tokenURI function by default, which may cause
integration issues.
Consider aligning these implementations with the Solidity library to ensure consistency and
mitigate potential risks.
Update: Resolved at commit 47d2d9c.

L-03 Missing Checks in ERC-20 Implementation
Some validation checks are missing in the current ERC-20 implementation when compared to
the Solidity library:
• In mod.rs , the _approve() function checks the spender's address but does not
verify that the owner's address is not zero, unlike in the Solidity library.

Contracts for Stylus Audit − Low Severity − 10

 • The _spend_allowance() function directly sets the allowance in storage without
calling the internal _approve() function, as is done in the Solidity version. This
bypasses the address validation checks (owner and spender) that _approve()
provides.
• The transfer_from() function currently calls _spend_allowance() before
_transfer() , where the latter includes non-zero address checks for both the sender
and recipient. However, these checks should be performed prior to updating the
allowance, as is done in the Solidity implementation, to prevent unnecessary storage
writes in the event of a revert.
Consider adding the aforementioned missing checks to improve the security of the library.

Functions
The pausable.rs contract exposes the pause and unpause functions as part of a

version of the Pausable contract, the corresponding functions are marked as internal .

pause and unpause , and ensures that proper access control measures are applied.

reducing the risk of unintended function access.

## Source-only audit cross-check

I checked every report item marked resolved against the current working tree. I did not edit files or run Cargo, so these are source checks, not test verification.

### v0.1

| Finding | Current status and evidence |
|---|---|
| M-01 — ERC-721 does not support ERC-165 | **Confirmed resolved:** `supports_interface` recognizes both ERC-721 and ERC-165 IDs in [erc721/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc721/mod.rs:514). |
| L-01 — Incomplete checkpoints implementation | **Confirmed resolved:** generic checkpoint storage is in [checkpoints/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/structs/checkpoints/mod.rs:52), with S160, S208, and S224 in [generic_size.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/structs/checkpoints/generic_size.rs:63). |
| L-02 — Inconsistent ERC-721 extensions | **Confirmed resolved:** URI storage checks token existence and composes the base URI in [uri_storage.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/uri_storage.rs:71); metadata checks ownership and implements token URI generation in [metadata.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/metadata.rs:101). |
| L-03 — Missing ERC-20 checks | **Partially resolved:** `_approve` checks zero owner and spender, and allowance spending goes through `_approve` in [erc20/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs:347) and [erc20/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs:562). However, `transfer_from` still spends allowance before `_transfer` checks `from` and `to` at [erc20/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs:314) and [erc20/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/mod.rs:392). A later revert rolls the storage change back, so this is a residual gas cost, not a persistent allowance change. |
| L-04 — Public pause/unpause exposure | **Confirmed resolved:** only `paused` is in the public trait; `pause` and `unpause` are inherent methods in [pausable.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/pausable.rs:79) and [pausable.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/pausable.rs:101). |
| N-01 — Unaddressed TODO/FIXME comments | **Residual:** the current tree still contains multiple TODOs without issue references, including in ERC-4626, ERC-721 extensions, and address utilities. The full current list is visible with `rg -n 'TODO|FIXME' contracts lib/crypto contracts-proc`; examples include [erc4626.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/erc4626.rs:869), [consecutive.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/consecutive.rs:186), and [address.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/address.rs:91). |
| N-03 — Unnecessary hash-pair swap | **Confirmed resolved:** `commutative_hash_pair` chooses argument order directly in [hash.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/hash.rs:152). |
| N-04 — Misleading Pausable “modifier” reference | **Confirmed resolved:** the API describes helper methods such as `when_not_paused` in [pausable.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/pausable.rs:134). |
| N-05 — Unused ECDSA error | **Confirmed resolved:** the error declarations include invalid signature and invalid S, but no signature-length error, in [ecdsa.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/cryptography/ecdsa.rs:30). |

### v0.2

| Finding | Current status and evidence |
|---|---|
| H-01 — Limb shift overflow | **Confirmed resolved:** both shift directions reject out-of-range shifts and use checked limb shifts in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:793) and [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:849). |
| M-01 — Potential underflow in `ct_rem` | **Confirmed resolved:** zero divisors are rejected and the remainder loop handles carry in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:1109). |
| L-01 — Custom Merkle hashes assume commutativity | **Confirmed resolved:** the custom-hasher docs require commutative construction in [merkle.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:149), and pair sorting is implemented in [hash.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/hash.rs:152). |
| L-02 — Carry/borrow type inconsistency | **Confirmed resolved:** `adc` and `sbb` take `bool` in [limb.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/limb.rs:85). |
| L-03 — Zero-bit ambiguity | **Confirmed resolved:** `num_bits()` returns one for zero in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:197). |
| L-04 — Hex parser overflow check | **Confirmed resolved:** `from_str_hex` checks the limb index before writing in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:1020). |
| L-05 — ERC-20 wrapper decimals | **Confirmed resolved:** decimals are read from the underlying token, with an 18-decimal fallback, in [wrapper.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/wrapper.rs:224). |
| L-06 — ERC-4626 read mutability | **Confirmed resolved:** view methods such as `total_assets` use `&self`; mutating methods such as `deposit` use `&mut self` in [erc4626.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/erc4626.rs:206) and [erc4626.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/extensions/erc4626.rs:369). |
| L-07 — Duplicate selectors in `interface_id` traits | **Confirmed resolved:** the macro emits pairwise selector-byte assertions, gated by method cfg attributes, in [interface_id.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts-proc/src/interface_id.rs:132). |
| L-08 — Dropped trait components in macro output | **Confirmed resolved:** the macro retains unsafety, generics, supertraits, and the where clause in [interface_id.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts-proc/src/interface_id.rs:31) and [interface_id.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts-proc/src/interface_id.rs:196). |
| L-09 — Big-integer timing side channel | **Source fix confirmed:** comparisons and `Ord::cmp` process the full limb loop rather than returning early, in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:103) and [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:683). I did not measure timing. |
| N-01 — `must_use` on Merkle verification | **Partial/style residual:** the boolean `verify` has an explicit attribute, but the multiproof functions do not in [merkle.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:59), [merkle.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:128), and [merkle.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/merkle.rs:263). Their `Result` return type is itself `must_use`, so ignored results still trigger the Rust lint. |
| N-02 — Redundant `adc` attribute | **Confirmed resolved:** the file-level lint allowance remains, while `adc` has no duplicate local allowance in [limb.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/limb.rs:4). |
| N-03 — Missing `inline(always)` | **Confirmed resolved:** the noted comparison helpers carry the attribute in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:103). |
| N-04 — Incorrect projective equality comment | **Confirmed resolved:** the corrected cross-product comment is in [sw/projective.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/curve/sw/projective.rs:69). |
| N-05 — Missing attribution | **Confirmed resolved:** Arkworks references appear in [curve/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/curve/mod.rs:3) and [field/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/field/mod.rs:5). |
| N-06 — Poseidon documentation | **Confirmed resolved:** padding/domain-separation responsibilities and mode transition behavior are documented in [poseidon2/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/poseidon2/mod.rs:7) and [poseidon2/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/poseidon2/mod.rs:142). |
| N-07 — Shift overflow semantics | **Confirmed resolved:** shifts panic when the amount reaches the bit width in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:793) and [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:849). |
| N-08 — Misleading interface-ID documentation | **Confirmed resolved:** generated docs describe `interface_id` as a function in [interface_id.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts-proc/src/interface_id.rs:204). |
| N-09 — Typographical errors | **Confirmed for cited examples:** the cited misspellings are absent from current source. |
| N-10 — Insufficient unit-test coverage | **Not marked resolved in the audit; acknowledged.** Coverage was not measured here. |

### v0.3

| Finding | Current status and evidence |
|---|---|
| H-01 — Bandersnatch/Jubjub parameters | **Source fix confirmed:** current generator and modulus constants are in [bandersnatch.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/bandersnatch.rs:15) and [jubjub.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/curve/te/instance/jubjub.rs:15). |
| M-01 — `ruint` byte padding | **Confirmed resolved:** conversion pads to the destination byte width before decoding in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:636); a regression case is present at [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:1452). |
| M-02 — Incorrect `into_u128` limb check | **Confirmed resolved:** the one-limb case is handled separately and higher limbs are checked in [uint.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/arithmetic/uint.rs:595). |
| M-03 — Incomplete expanded-secret zeroization | **Confirmed resolved:** `ExpandedSecretKey` derives `ZeroizeOnDrop` in [eddsa.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/eddsa.rs:86). |
| M-04 — P-256 signature malleability | **Confirmed resolved:** `s > n/2` is rejected before calling the precompile in [p256_verify.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/precompiles/p256_verify.rs:11). |
| L-01 — `AdminChanged` event indexing | **Confirmed resolved:** neither event parameter is indexed in [erc1967/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/proxy/erc1967/mod.rs:30). |
| L-02 — Edwards batch normalization | **Confirmed resolved:** zero projective Z is rejected and identity handling is explicit in [te/projective.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/curve/te/projective.rs:213). |
| L-03 — UUPS implementation context | **Source fix confirmed:** a dedicated logic flag, nonzero ERC-1967 implementation slot, and proxy-stored version check are used in [uups_upgradeable.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:74) and [uups_upgradeable.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:460). |
| L-04 — Safe ERC-20 allowance fallback behavior | **Confirmed resolved:** no-code tokens fail, and allowance uses a typed high-level call in [safe_erc20.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/utils/safe_erc20.rs:625). |
| L-05 — `*_relaxed` behavior | **Confirmed resolved:** recipient fallback behavior is explicit; contract recipients require a token contract and successful `true` result in [safe_erc20.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc20/utils/safe_erc20.rs:460). |
| N-01 — Zero-Z affine conversion panic | **Confirmed resolved:** conversion now has an explicit panic message in [te/affine.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/curve/te/affine.rs:233). |
| N-02 — Missing ranged `values` | **Confirmed implemented:** `values_slice(start, end)` clamps the range and returns that slice in [enumerable_set/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/structs/enumerable_set/mod.rs:189). Its docs at line 197 say it copies the entire storage, which is inaccurate for the ranged implementation. |
| N-03 — Inconsistent public-key use in EdDSA | **Confirmed resolved:** `compute_R` hashes and uses the local `A` public-key value in [eddsa.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/eddsa.rs:387). |
| N-04 — Scalar/WideScalar parameter equality | **Confirmed resolved:** wide parameters derive generator and modulus from the scalar parameters in [eddsa.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/eddsa.rs:40). |
| N-05 — Enumerable gas warnings | **Confirmed resolved:** warnings cover full-set reads and clearing in [enumerable_set/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/utils/structs/enumerable_set/mod.rs:96) and role-member reads in [access/control/extensions/enumerable.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/access/control/extensions/enumerable.rs:81). |
| N-06 — EdDSA byte/bit typo | **Confirmed resolved:** the panic text says 32 bytes in [eddsa.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/eddsa.rs:260). |
| N-07 — Compressed-point MSB assumption | **Confirmed resolved:** the base field’s spare-bit condition is compile-time asserted in [eddsa.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/eddsa.rs:254). |

## Remaining audit-related concerns

No unresolved high-severity item from the reports marked resolved stood out in this source review. Open or partial items worth carrying into the final review:

- **v0.2 M-02, acknowledged Medium:** custom selectors in an `#[interface_id]` trait are still not checked against selectors on `#[public]` implementations. The macro consumes trait selector attributes at [interface_id.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts-proc/src/interface_id.rs:48), but there is no implementation-selector comparison.
- **v0.2 Poseidon2 recommendations:** the exponent permutation check is present, but round-count parity and minimum security rounds are not enforced. The implementation checks only the S-box exponent in [poseidon2/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/poseidon2/mod.rs:62); parameters and round counts remain the implementer’s responsibility in [params.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/poseidon2/params.rs:11).
- **Acknowledged findings remain open:** v0.1 L-05, L-06, N-02; v0.2 M-02 and N-10.  
- The v0.1 L-03 call ordering, v0.1 N-01 TODOs, and v0.2 N-01 explicit-attribute gap are residuals in lower-risk areas; none implies a demonstrated asset-loss path from this source review.

   191	impl Erc721Wrapper {
   192	    fn ensure_underlying_has_code(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
   193	        let token = self.underlying();
   194	        if self.vm().code_size(token) == 0 {
   195	            return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(Erc721FailedOperation {
   196	                token,
   197	            }));
   198	        }
   199	
   200	        Ok(())
   201	    }
   202	
   203	    /// Constructor.
   204	    ///
   205	    /// # Arguments
   206	    ///
   207	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
   208	    /// * `underlying_token` - The wrapped token.
   209	    pub fn constructor(&mut self, underlying_token: Address) {
   210	        self.underlying.set(underlying_token);
   211	    }
   212	
   213	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::deposit_for()`] for more information.
   214	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
   215	    pub fn deposit_for(
   216	        &mut self,
   217	        account: Address,
   218	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
   219	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
   220	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
   221	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
   222	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
   223	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
   224	
   225	        if !token_ids.is_empty() {
   226	            self.ensure_underlying_has_code()?;
   227	        }
   228	
   229	        for token_id in token_ids {
   230	            // This is an "unsafe" transfer that doesn't call any hook on
   231	            // the receiver. With [`IErc721Wrapper::underlying()`] being trusted
   232	            // (by design of this contract) and no other contracts expected to
   233	            // be called from there, we are safe.
   234	            let call = Call::new_mutating(self);
   235	            match underlying.transfer_from(
   236	                self.vm(),
   237	                call,
   238	                sender,
   239	                contract_address,
   240	                token_id,
   241	            ) {
   242	                Ok(()) => (),
   243	                Err(e) => {
   244	                    if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
   245	                        if !reason.is_empty() {
   246	                            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
   247	                                erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason {
   248	                                    reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
   249	                                        .to_string(),
   250	                                },
   251	                            ));
   252	                        }
   253	                    }
   254	                    return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(
   255	                        Erc721FailedOperation { token: self.underlying() },
   256	                    ));
   257	                }
   258	            }
   259	
   260	            erc721._safe_mint(account, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
   261	        }
   262	
   263	        Ok(true)
   264	    }
   265	
   266	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::withdraw_to()`] for more information.
   267	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
   268	    pub fn withdraw_to(
   269	        &mut self,
   270	        account: Address,
   271	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
   272	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
   273	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
   274	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
   275	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
   276	
   277	        if !token_ids.is_empty() {
   278	            self.ensure_underlying_has_code()?;
   279	        }
   280	
   281	        for token_id in token_ids {
   282	            // Setting the `auth` argument enables the `_is_authorized` check
   283	            // which verifies that the token exists (from != 0).
   284	            // Therefore, it is not needed to verify that the return value is
   285	            // not 0 here.
   286	            erc721._update(Address::ZERO, token_id, sender)?;
   287	            let call = Call::new_mutating(self);
   288	            match underlying.safe_transfer_from(
   289	                self.vm(),
   290	                call,
   291	                self.vm().contract_address(),
   292	                account,
   293	                token_id,
   294	                vec![].into(),
   295	            ) {
   296	                Ok(()) => (),
   297	                Err(e) => {
   298	                    if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
   299	                        if !reason.is_empty() {
   300	                            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
   301	                                erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason {
   302	                                    reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
   303	                                        .to_string(),
   304	                                },
   305	                            ));
   306	                        }
   307	                    }
   308	                    return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(
   309	                        Erc721FailedOperation { token: self.underlying() },
   310	                    ));
   311	                }
   312	            }
   313	        }
   314	
   315	        Ok(true)
   316	    }

   319	    ///
   320	    /// # Arguments
   321	    ///
   322	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
   323	    /// * `operator` - The operator of the transfer.
   324	    /// * `from` - The sender of the transfer.
   325	    /// * `token_id` - The token id of the transfer.
   326	    /// * `data` - The data of the transfer.
   327	    /// * `erc721` - Write access to an [`Erc721`] contract.
   328	    ///
   329	    /// # Errors
   330	    ///
   331	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If `self.vm().msg_sender()` is not the underlying
   332	    ///   token.
   333	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
   334	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
   335	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
   336	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
   337	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
   338	    pub fn on_erc721_received(
   339	        &mut self,
   340	        _operator: Address,
   341	        from: Address,
   342	        token_id: U256,
   343	        _data: &Bytes,
   344	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
   345	    ) -> Result<B32, Error> {
   346	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
   347	        if self.underlying() != sender || self.vm().code_size(sender) == 0 {
   348	            return Err(Error::UnsupportedToken(ERC721UnsupportedToken {
   349	                token: sender,
   350	            }));
   351	        }
   352	
   353	        erc721._safe_mint(from, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
   354	
   355	        Ok(RECEIVER_FN_SELECTOR)
   356	    }

   364	    /// Mints wrapped tokens to cover any underlying tokens that would have been
   365	    /// function that can be exposed with access control if desired.
   366	    ///
   367	    /// # Arguments
   368	    ///
   369	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
   370	    /// * `account` - The account to mint tokens to.
   371	    /// * `token_id` - A mutable reference to the Erc20 contract.
   372	    /// * `erc721` - Write access to an [`Erc721`] contract.
   373	    ///
   374	    /// # Errors
   375	    ///
   376	    /// * [`Error::Erc721FailedOperation`] - If the underlying token is not a
   377	    ///   [`Erc721`] or the contract fails to execute the call.
   378	    /// * [`Error::IncorrectOwner`] - If the underlying token is not owned by
   379	    ///   the contract.
   380	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
   381	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
   382	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
   383	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
   384	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
   385	    fn _recover(
   386	        &mut self,
   387	        account: Address,
   388	        token_id: U256,
   389	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
   390	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
   391	        self.ensure_underlying_has_code()?;
   392	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
   393	
   394	        let owner = underlying
   395	            .owner_of(self.vm(), Call::new(), token_id)
   396	            .map_err(|_| {
   397	                Error::Erc721FailedOperation(Erc721FailedOperation {
   398	                    token: self.underlying(),
   399	                })
   400	            })?;
   401	
   402	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
   403	        if owner != contract_address {
   404	            return Err(erc721::Error::IncorrectOwner(
   405	                erc721::ERC721IncorrectOwner {
   406	                    sender: contract_address,
   407	                    token_id,
   408	                    owner,
   409	                },
   410	            )
   411	            .into());
   412	        }
   413	
   414	        erc721._safe_mint(account, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
   415	
   416	        Ok(token_id)
   417	    }
   418	}

   324	    /// Mint wrapped token to cover any underlying tokens that would have been
   325	    /// transferred by mistake or acquired from rebasing mechanisms.
   326	    ///
   327	    /// Internal function that can be exposed with access control if desired.
   328	    ///
   329	    /// # Arguments
   330	    ///
   331	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
   332	    /// * `account` - The account to mint tokens to.
   333	    /// * `erc20` - Write access to an [`Erc20`] contract.
   334	    ///
   335	    /// # Errors
   336	    ///
   337	    /// * [`Error::InvalidUnderlying`]  - If the external call for
   338	    ///   [`IErc20::balance_of`] fails.
   339	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If the `account` address is
   340	    ///   [`Address::ZERO`].
   341	    ///
   342	    /// # Panics
   343	    ///
   344	    /// * If the underlying balance is less than the [`IErc20::total_supply`].
   345	    pub fn _recover(
   346	        &mut self,
   347	        account: Address,
   348	        erc20: &mut Erc20,
   349	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
   350	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
   351	
   352	        let underlying_token = Erc20Interface::new(self.underlying());
   353	
   354	        let underlying_balance = underlying_token
   355	            .balance_of(self.vm(), Call::new(), contract_address)
   356	            .map_err(|_| ERC20InvalidUnderlying { token: self.underlying() })?;
   357	
   358	        let value = underlying_balance
   359	            .checked_sub(erc20.total_supply())
   360	            .expect("underlying balance should be greater than the `IErc20::total_supply`");
   361	
   362	        if value > U256::ZERO {
   363	            erc20._mint(account, value)?;
   364	        }
   365	
   366	        Ok(value)
   367	    }
   368	}

   192	    fn ensure_underlying_has_code(&self) -> Result<(), Error> {
   193	        let token = self.underlying();
   194	        if self.vm().code_size(token) == 0 {
   195	            return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(Erc721FailedOperation {
   196	                token,
   197	            }));
   198	        }
   199	
   200	        Ok(())
   201	    }

   203	    /// Constructor.
   204	    ///
   205	    /// # Arguments
   206	    ///
   207	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
   208	    /// * `underlying_token` - The wrapped token.
   209	    pub fn constructor(&mut self, underlying_token: Address) {

   213	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::deposit_for()`] for more information.
   214	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
   215	    pub fn deposit_for(
   216	        &mut self,
   217	        account: Address,
   218	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
   219	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
   220	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
   221	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
   222	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
   223	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
   224	
   225	        if !token_ids.is_empty() {
   226	            self.ensure_underlying_has_code()?;
   227	        }
   228	
   229	        for token_id in token_ids {
   230	            // This is an "unsafe" transfer that doesn't call any hook on
   231	            // the receiver. With [`IErc721Wrapper::underlying()`] being trusted
   232	            // (by design of this contract) and no other contracts expected to
   233	            // be called from there, we are safe.
   234	            let call = Call::new_mutating(self);
   235	            match underlying.transfer_from(
   236	                self.vm(),
   237	                call,
   238	                sender,
   239	                contract_address,
   240	                token_id,
   241	            ) {
   242	                Ok(()) => (),
   243	                Err(e) => {
   244	                    if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
   245	                        if !reason.is_empty() {
   246	                            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
   247	                                erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason {
   248	                                    reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
   249	                                        .to_string(),
   250	                                },
   251	                            ));
   252	                        }
   253	                    }
   254	                    return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(
   255	                        Erc721FailedOperation { token: self.underlying() },
   256	                    ));
   257	                }
   258	            }
   259	
   260	            erc721._safe_mint(account, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
   261	        }
   262	
   263	        Ok(true)
   264	    }

   266	    /// Check [`IErc721Wrapper::withdraw_to()`] for more information.
   267	    #[allow(clippy::missing_errors_doc)]
   268	    pub fn withdraw_to(
   269	        &mut self,
   270	        account: Address,
   271	        token_ids: Vec<U256>,
   272	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
   273	    ) -> Result<bool, Error> {
   274	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
   275	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
   276	
   277	        if !token_ids.is_empty() {
   278	            self.ensure_underlying_has_code()?;
   279	        }
   280	
   281	        for token_id in token_ids {
   282	            // Setting the `auth` argument enables the `_is_authorized` check
   283	            // which verifies that the token exists (from != 0).
   284	            // Therefore, it is not needed to verify that the return value is
   285	            // not 0 here.
   286	            erc721._update(Address::ZERO, token_id, sender)?;
   287	            let call = Call::new_mutating(self);
   288	            match underlying.safe_transfer_from(
   289	                self.vm(),
   290	                call,
   291	                self.vm().contract_address(),
   292	                account,
   293	                token_id,
   294	                vec![].into(),
   295	            ) {
   296	                Ok(()) => (),
   297	                Err(e) => {
   298	                    if let stylus_sdk::stylus_core::calls::errors::Error::Revert(ref reason) = e {
   299	                        if !reason.is_empty() {
   300	                            return Err(Error::InvalidReceiverWithReason(
   301	                                erc721::InvalidReceiverWithReason {
   302	                                    reason: String::from_utf8_lossy(reason)
   303	                                        .to_string(),
   304	                                },
   305	                            ));
   306	                        }
   307	                    }
   308	                    return Err(Error::Erc721FailedOperation(
   309	                        Erc721FailedOperation { token: self.underlying() },
   310	                    ));
   311	                }
   312	            }
   313	        }
   314	
   315	        Ok(true)
   316	    }

   325	    /// * `token_id` - The token id of the transfer.
   326	    /// * `data` - The data of the transfer.
   327	    /// * `erc721` - Write access to an [`Erc721`] contract.
   328	    ///
   329	    /// # Errors
   330	    ///
   331	    /// * [`Error::UnsupportedToken`] - If `self.vm().msg_sender()` is not the underlying
   332	    ///   token.
   333	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
   334	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
   335	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
   336	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
   337	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
   338	    pub fn on_erc721_received(
   339	        &mut self,
   340	        _operator: Address,
   341	        from: Address,
   342	        token_id: U256,
   343	        _data: &Bytes,
   344	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
   345	    ) -> Result<B32, Error> {
   346	        let sender = self.vm().msg_sender();
   347	        if self.underlying() != sender || self.vm().code_size(sender) == 0 {
   348	            return Err(Error::UnsupportedToken(ERC721UnsupportedToken {
   349	                token: sender,
   350	            }));
   351	        }
   352	
   353	        erc721._safe_mint(from, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
   354	
   355	        Ok(RECEIVER_FN_SELECTOR)
   356	    }

   364	    /// Mints wrapped tokens to cover any underlying tokens that would have been
   365	    /// function that can be exposed with access control if desired.
   366	    ///
   367	    /// # Arguments
   368	    ///
   369	    /// * `&mut self` - Write access to the contract's state.
   370	    /// * `account` - The account to mint tokens to.
   371	    /// * `token_id` - A mutable reference to the Erc20 contract.
   372	    /// * `erc721` - Write access to an [`Erc721`] contract.
   373	    ///
   374	    /// # Errors
   375	    ///
   376	    /// * [`Error::Erc721FailedOperation`] - If the underlying token is not a
   377	    ///   [`Erc721`] or the contract fails to execute the call.
   378	    /// * [`Error::IncorrectOwner`] - If the underlying token is not owned by
   379	    ///   the contract.
   380	    /// * [`Error::InvalidSender`] - If `token_id` already exists.
   381	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If `to` is [`Address::ZERO`].
   382	    /// * [`Error::InvalidReceiver`] - If
   383	    ///   [`erc721::IErc721Receiver::on_erc721_received`] hasn't returned its
   384	    ///   interface id or returned with an error.
   385	    fn _recover(
   386	        &mut self,
   387	        account: Address,
   388	        token_id: U256,
   389	        erc721: &mut Erc721,
   390	    ) -> Result<U256, Error> {
   391	        self.ensure_underlying_has_code()?;
   392	        let underlying = Erc721Interface::new(self.underlying());
   393	
   394	        let owner = underlying
   395	            .owner_of(self.vm(), Call::new(), token_id)
   396	            .map_err(|_| {
   397	                Error::Erc721FailedOperation(Erc721FailedOperation {
   398	                    token: self.underlying(),
   399	                })
   400	            })?;
   401	
   402	        let contract_address = self.vm().contract_address();
   403	        if owner != contract_address {
   404	            return Err(erc721::Error::IncorrectOwner(
   405	                erc721::ERC721IncorrectOwner {
   406	                    sender: contract_address,
   407	                    token_id,
   408	                    owner,
   409	                },
   410	            )
   411	            .into());
   412	        }
   413	
   414	        erc721._safe_mint(account, token_id, &vec![].into())?;
   415	
   416	        Ok(token_id)
   417	    }
   418	}

You are in a clone of OpenZeppelin rust-contracts-stylus at release v0.3.0.

Goal: Stylus developers should be able to build contracts on this library with the
latest SDK, trust them with real money, and upgrade to it without surprises. Get the
whole library there.

Start by migrating it to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on stable Rust 1.91.0.

Scope: the whole library. All contracts and extensions, contracts-proc, lib/crypto,
all examples, benches, fuzz targets and docs pages. lib/e2e and lib/e2e-proc are the
old E2E framework; the SDK's devnet tooling replaces them. Nothing is out of scope and
nothing may be commented out.

The migration must:
- replace global accessors with VM accessors,
- replace motsu with the Stylus testing framework,
- move the E2E tests to the SDK's devnet tooling,
- keep the benches working,
- keep the public ABI and behavior, unless a design change you document needs otherwise.

Done means: everything in scope builds and passes clippy and fmt. No global accessors,
no motsu. All unit tests, E2E tests and benches pass. Unit-test coverage is not lower
than on v0.3.0. Every E2E scenario from v0.3.0, success and failure, is still tested.
Storage layout stays compatible for contracts deployed behind a proxy, or every change
is in the upgrade guide. Every example in scope fits the WASM size limit and activates on
the devnet.

Then go further.

Use the new SDK fully:
- Read what changed in the Stylus SDK between 0.9.0 and 0.10.10. Use every change that
  makes this library better. Don't stop at making the old code compile.

Priorities for every design and refactor choice, in this order:
1. Developer experience: how easily consumers of the library compose the contracts and
   extensions in their own contracts.
2. Gas costs: measure them with the benches, before and after.
3. WASM size: every contract must fit the limit. Beyond that, size is not a goal.

Developers:
- Redesign the extensions where it makes them simpler to use and compose. Study how
  OpenZeppelin's Solidity, Cairo, Stellar and Sui Move contracts solve the same problems.
- Write the upgrade guide a developer on v0.3.0 needs: every breaking change and what
  to do about it.

Code:
- Apply KISS, SOLID and DRY to the code and tests. Merge examples and duplicate tests
  where no scenario is lost.
- Make rustdoc and the docs pages correct and consistent for the new API.

Evidence:
- Use the tools the best Rust security engineers use, not only unit tests: fuzzing or
  property tests, and differential tests against v0.3.0 behavior.
- Don't use mutation testing or formal verification (no cargo-mutants, no Kani).
- Aim for 100% coverage of the code in scope. It is reachable.

Security:
- Do a full security review of the code in scope. Look for what the reports in
  audits/ missed.
- List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
- Describe every new finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact and the
  severity.
- For each new bug, commit a failing PoC test first and the fix in a separate commit.
- Don't trust audits/. Check that every finding marked as resolved is really fixed.

Before you start:
- Check the environment. List every tool you will need for the whole task, including
  the evidence tools, with the version you found.
- Check that Docker is running.
- If anything is missing or has the wrong version, stop. Print what is missing and what
  you need, and do nothing else. Don't install anything yourself.
- If nothing is missing, say so and start.

How to work:
- After the check passes, work autonomously. Do not ask questions. When you face a decision, pick the best
  option, write down why, and move on.
- Plan the work yourself and use as many sub-agents as you need.
- Don't judge your own work. Trust only what a tool shows: a build, a test, a fuzzer.
- Don't stop until the migration is done and every check passes. If something in scope
  can't be made to work, say so. Don't hide it.
- Commit in small logical steps.

At the end write two files:
- MIGRATION.md: what changed and why, every decision, design changes, SDK features
  you adopted, gas and WASM size before and after, the evidence you produced, and the

I’ll review `lib/crypto` and `contracts-proc` for actionable issues beyond the audit inventory, tracing security-sensitive invariants and macro expansion paths. I’ll only inspect source and will not run Cargo or edit files.

Read-only review of `lib/crypto` and `contracts-proc` found three candidates beyond the numbered audit findings:

1. **EdDSA accepts the identity verifying key** — Medium, conditional on a consumer accepting an attacker-supplied or default key. With `VerifyingKey::from_affine(AffinePoint::zero())`, a signature using `R = B` and `s = 1` verifies for any message because `kA = 0`. `VerifyingKey::default()` also creates the identity. Suggested PoC and source locations were sent to the parent. Reject identity keys and validate public inputs.

2. **Secret-dependent timing in EdDSA signing paths** — Medium where timing or gas is observable. Curve scalar multiplication branches on scalar bits, and signing normalizes secret-derived points through variable-time field inversion. Suggested instrumentation: compare point-add counts for equal-width scalars with differing Hamming weights. Use constant-time multiplication and inversion or avoid exposing these paths as suitable for secret operations.

3. **`#[interface_id]` ignores method-level `cfg`** — Low. A cfg-disabled method still contributes to the generated interface ID, and its selector collision checks can still fail the build. Suggested PoC: compare the ID with and without a feature-gated method, and compile a disabled colliding method pair. Apply method cfg conditions to selector terms and checks, or reject conditional methods.

I found no additional actionable issue in the inspected Merkle verification, generic hash routines, built-in Pedersen parameters, Poseidon2 execution, or bigint/field/curve correctness beyond the timing concern. I did not run Cargo or edit files.

The timing leak is **not an actionable on-chain confidentiality finding for this tree’s current Stylus use**. The code is variable-time, but this repository uses `SigningKey` and `sign()` only in crypto tests and E2E tests; the Stylus EdDSA example exposes verification only. A contract that signs with a private key would already expose that key through its code, storage, or calldata.

The implementation does branch on secret-derived bits: EdDSA key derivation and signing multiply the generator by secret scalars ([eddsa.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/eddsa.rs:172), [te/mod.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/curve/te/mod.rs:66)). Signing also normalizes a secret-derived point through variable-time field inversion ([fp.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/field/fp.rs:142), [affine.rs](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/curve/te/affine.rs:233)). Stylus meters WASM computation in ink and exposes ink usage, so branch-dependent work can affect observable cost; that does not create secrecy for on-chain keys ([Arbitrum gas metering docs](https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/concepts/gas-metering), [Stylus execution model](https://docs.arbitrum.io/stylus/gentle-introduction)).

For the Stylus-only threat model, document signing as variable-time and off-chain only. If the crate promises secure signing for host applications too, the fix must cover scalar multiplication, field arithmetic, and point normalization end to end; changing only the scalar-multiplication branch would be incomplete.

content.text:
Source-only review found four actionable candidates and one composition warning. I made no edits and ran no Cargo commands.

| Finding | Severity | Trigger and impact | Evidence / test gap | Audit status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Beacon proxy stores its beacon in colliding application storage | High | A delegated implementation writes the same ordinary storage slot as `BeaconProxy.beacon`. Initialization can overwrite an implementation’s first scalar field; a later write can replace the beacon address and permanently break implementation lookup, locking proxy assets. | [`proxy.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/proxy/beacon/proxy.rs:31) stores `beacon` as `StorageAddress`; the constructor delegate-initializes, then writes it at lines 65–72. Implementation lookup reads that field at lines 86–90. `Erc1967Utils` already stores the beacon in the collision-resistant ERC-1967 slot at [`utils.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/proxy/erc1967/utils.rs:363). Existing proxy tests do not cover an implementation with a scalar at the colliding slot. | Not found in the v0.1–v0.3 reports I checked. |
| UUPS example initializer can transfer proxy ownership to any caller | High | After proxy initialization, an attacker calls `initialize(attacker)`. `set_version` accepts the already-current version, then `Ownable::constructor` overwrites the owner; the attacker can upgrade to malicious logic. | Example initializer: [`uups-proxy/src/lib.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/examples/uups-proxy/src/lib.rs:109); same pattern in v2 at [`uups-proxy-new-version/src/lib.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/examples/uups-proxy-new-version/src/lib.rs:129). `set_version` allows the same version at [`uups_upgradeable.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/proxy/utils/uups_upgradeable.rs:385), and `Ownable::constructor` resets ownership. E2E tests already expect replay rejection at [`uups-proxy.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/examples/uups-proxy/tests/uups-proxy.rs:181), but the current implementation has no such guard; `InvalidInitialization` is only declared/mapped. | Not found in the audit reports. |
| ERC-721 owner enumeration treats token ID 0 as out of bounds | Low | A valid token ID 0 stored at an owner index is returned as an out-of-bounds error, preventing consumers from enumerating that token. | [`enumerable.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/enumerable.rs:146) uses zero as the missing-value sentinel. The success test covers ID 1 only at lines 628–668. | Not found in the audit reports. |
| EdDSA example accepts non-canonical signature encodings | Low | Adding the Curve25519 scalar modulus to valid `s` still verifies because the ABI input is reduced modulo the scalar field. This gives multiple accepted encodings for one signature and can defeat applications that replay-track raw signature bytes. | [`eddsa/src/lib.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/examples/eddsa/src/lib.rs:29) reduces public-key coordinates and `s`; reduction is explicit in [`fp.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/lib/crypto/src/field/fp.rs:491). Existing E2E coverage uses canonical encoding and wrong-message rejection only. | Separate from the v0.3 EdDSA findings; not found in the reports. |

`ERC721Consecutive::_mint_consecutive` also has no constructor-context check despite its docs describing constructor-only use ([`consecutive.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/consecutive.rs:374)). If a consumer exposes it at runtime, it emits `ConsecutiveTransfer` without per-token `Transfer` events or receiver checks. This is a conditional compliance and integration risk; either enforce the context or state clearly that callers must enforce it.

I found no concrete reentrancy theft in the inspected ERC-4626, wrapper, flash-mint, vesting-release, ERC-721 receiver, or ERC-1155 receiver flows. State updates precede outgoing callbacks/transfers where needed. ERC-20/721/1155 accounting, role administration, vesting release accounting, proxy validation/version checks, checkpoint ordering, bitmap/set invariants, Merkle proof queue bounds, and EIP-712/ECDSA/P256 validation were also traced.

Two composition risks should be explicit in the upgrade guide and example docs: adding ERC-721 Enumerable or AccessControl Enumerable to an existing proxy leaves historical enumeration data uninitialized; several minting examples are intentionally permissionless and are not production templates.

`ERC721Consecutive::_mint_consecutive` also has no constructor-context check despite its docs describing constructor-only use ([`consecutive.rs`](/tmp/bench/ws/contracts/src/token/erc721/extensions/consecutive.rs:374)). If a consumer exposes it at runtime, it emits `ConsecutiveTransfer` without per-token `Transfer` events or receiver checks. This is a conditional compliance and integration risk; either enforce the context or state clearly that callers must enforce it.

I found no concrete reentrancy theft in the inspected ERC-4626, wrapper, flash-mint, vesting-release, ERC-721 receiver, or ERC-1155 receiver flows. State updates precede outgoing callbacks/transfers where needed. ERC-20/721/1155 accounting, role administration, vesting release accounting, proxy validation/version checks, checkpoint ordering, bitmap/set invariants, Merkle proof queue bounds, and EIP-712/ECDSA/P256 validation were also traced.

Two composition risks should be explicit in the upgrade guide and example docs: adding ERC-721 Enumerable or AccessControl Enumerable to an existing proxy leaves historical enumeration data uninitialized; several minting examples are intentionally permissionless and are not production templates.

You are in a clone of OpenZeppelin rust-contracts-stylus at release v0.3.0.

Goal: Stylus developers should be able to build contracts on this library with the
latest SDK, trust them with real money, and upgrade to it without surprises. Get the
whole library there.

Start by migrating it to Stylus SDK 0.10.10 on stable Rust 1.91.0.

Scope: the whole library. All contracts and extensions, contracts-proc, lib/crypto,
all examples, benches, fuzz targets and docs pages. lib/e2e and lib/e2e-proc are the
old E2E framework; the SDK's devnet tooling replaces them. Nothing is out of scope and
nothing may be commented out.

The migration must:
- replace global accessors with VM accessors,
- replace motsu with the Stylus testing framework,
- move the E2E tests to the SDK's devnet tooling,
- keep the benches working,
- keep the public ABI and behavior, unless a design change you document needs otherwise.

Done means: everything in scope builds and passes clippy and fmt. No global accessors,
no motsu. All unit tests, E2E tests and benches pass. Unit-test coverage is not lower
than on v0.3.0. Every E2E scenario from v0.3.0, success and failure, is still tested.
Storage layout stays compatible for contracts deployed behind a proxy, or every change
is in the upgrade guide. Every example in scope fits the WASM size limit and activates on
the devnet.

Then go further.

Use the new SDK fully:
- Read what changed in the Stylus SDK between 0.9.0 and 0.10.10. Use every change that
  makes this library better. Don't stop at making the old code compile.

Priorities for every design and refactor choice, in this order:
1. Developer experience: how easily consumers of the library compose the contracts and
   extensions in their own contracts.
2. Gas costs: measure them with the benches, before and after.
3. WASM size: every contract must fit the limit. Beyond that, size is not a goal.

Developers:
- Redesign the extensions where it makes them simpler to use and compose. Study how
  OpenZeppelin's Solidity, Cairo, Stellar and Sui Move contracts solve the same problems.
- Write the upgrade guide a developer on v0.3.0 needs: every breaking change and what
  to do about it.

Code:
- Apply KISS, SOLID and DRY to the code and tests. Merge examples and duplicate tests
  where no scenario is lost.
- Make rustdoc and the docs pages correct and consistent for the new API.

Evidence:
- Use the tools the best Rust security engineers use, not only unit tests: fuzzing or
  property tests, and differential tests against v0.3.0 behavior.
- Don't use mutation testing or formal verification (no cargo-mutants, no Kani).
- Aim for 100% coverage of the code in scope. It is reachable.

Security:
- Do a full security review of the code in scope. Look for what the reports in
  audits/ missed.
- List the invariants of each contract, then try to break each one.
- Describe every new finding: what breaks, how to trigger it, the impact and the
  severity.
- For each new bug, commit a failing PoC test first and the fix in a separate commit.
- Don't trust audits/. Check that every finding marked as resolved is really fixed.

Before you start:
- Check the environment. List every tool you will need for the whole task, including
  the evidence tools, with the version you found.
- Check that Docker is running.
- If anything is missing or has the wrong version, stop. Print what is missing and what
  you need, and do nothing else. Don't install anything yourself.
- If nothing is missing, say so and start.

How to work:
- After the check passes, work autonomously. Do not ask questions. When you face a decision, pick the best
  option, write down why, and move on.
- Plan the work yourself and use as many sub-agents as you need.
- Don't judge your own work. Trust only what a tool shows: a build, a test, a fuzzer.
- Don't stop until the migration is done and every check passes. If something in scope
  can't be made to work, say so. Don't hide it.
- Commit in small logical steps.

At the end write two files:
- MIGRATION.md: what changed and why, every decision, design changes, SDK features
  you adopted, gas and WASM size before and after, the evidence you produced, and the
  final output of all checks.
- SECURITY-REVIEW.md: scope, invariants, every finding (severity, description,
  impact, PoC, fix, and whether it is new or already in audits/), and the audit
  findings you checked.
